name: Re-admit a former student onto their existing record
priorityReason: Families leave and return every session. Without this the school ends up with two records for one child.

goal.actor: a returning family and the school
goal.capability: to rejoin without being asked again for what the school already holds
goal.outcome: the child comes back onto the same record, with their history still attached

secondaryActors.involvement: The same actors as a regular admission. The only difference is that no admission form is sent.
Reviews the inquiry, confirms the match to the former record, and schedules the admission test.

additional.description: The family ticks Re-admission on the inquiry form and gives the previous student ID.
A staff member records a phone or walk-in enquiry and marks it as a re-admission.

preconditions.condition: A student record exists at status Left, Struck off or Transferred, carrying the student ID the family quoted.
An inquiry exists with Re-admission ticked and a previous student ID entered.
An academic session is open and a class with capacity exists to return into.

establishedBy.name: Class, section and academic session structure

postConditions: The inquiry is attached to the existing student record, so everyone downstream knows this is a return and not a new child.
No admission-form invite is issued and no admission form is completed, because the school already holds the information.
On confirmation the existing student record is reactivated and linked to the new class and academic session.
The student keeps their original student ID and roll number, so fee, attendance and examination history stay joined to them.
The previous enrolment is closed rather than deleted, and the gap between leaving and returning stays visible on the record.
No second student record, guardian account or family code is created.
Where the previous student ID matched nothing, the inquiry proceeds as an ordinary new admission instead, with the admission form sent as usual.

screens.name: Inquiry review, re-admission match
actions: Reject match and treat as new admission

businessRules.rule: A re-admission reuses the existing student record. A second record for the same child is the failure this use case exists to prevent.
The previous student ID entered by the family is matched against former student records. A match is a proposal, not a fact.
The match is confirmed by the School Admin at review before anything proceeds. An unconfirmed or mismatched ID is resolved there, not later.

Because the school already holds the information, no admission-form invite is issued and no admission form is completed. Every other step — review, approval, test scheduling, marking and decision — happens exactly as for a new admission.

On confirmation the existing record is reactivated and linked to the new class and academic session. The student keeps their original student ID and roll number, so their history stays joined to them.
The return class defaults to the class above the one they left, which is usually right and is always overridable. It is a suggestion, never applied silently.
The previous enrolment is closed, not deleted. Attendance, marks and fee history from it stay attached and readable.
Any outstanding balance from the previous enrolment is shown to the Principal before the decision, because it is a fact that bears on whether the school wants the family back.
Where the guardian's contact changed while they were away, updating it here also changes their sign-in contact, since a guardian ID is tied to the family code.
A student who transferred to another branch is handled by inter-branch transfer, not here.
The gap between leaving and returning is preserved on the record. A re-admission never rewrites history to look continuous.
Where the previous student ID matches nothing and the family cannot supply a correct one, the inquiry continues as an ordinary new admission and the admission form is sent as usual.

transitions.condition: The match is confirmed at inquiry review (BR-3).
The match is confirmed, with the striking-off shown to the approver.
The re-admission is approved and a return class and section with capacity are assigned (UC-02-07).
Refused. The record returns to its previous status.

basicFlow.navigation: Public website → Inquiry form → Re-admission section
basicFlow.userAction: Ticks Re-admission and enters the previous student ID, year last attended and reason for leaving.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the extra fields that case needs and records the inquiry as a re-admission.
Matches the entry against former student records and attaches the proposed match to the inquiry.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Inquiry review → Re-admission match
basicFlow.userAction: Compares the inquiry against the matched record, field by field, and confirms the match.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Links the inquiry to the existing student record and marks it a confirmed re-admission.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews and forwards the inquiry in the ordinary way.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sets the inquiry to Forwarded to Principal, exactly as for a new admission.
Approves it, and issues no admission-form invite because the school already holds the information.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Applicants awaiting a test → Schedule test
basicFlow.userAction: Schedules the admission test as for any other applicant.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sends the date and time to the number on the inquiry, exactly as for a new admission.

basicFlow.userAction: Approves the admission after the test is marked.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Reactivates the existing record, closes the previous enrolment, creates the new one, and keeps the original student ID and roll number.

alternateFlows.condition: The previous student ID matches nothing
alternateFlows.navigation: Inquiry review → Reject match and treat as new admission
alternateFlows.behaviour: The admin resolves it — by correcting the ID, or by treating the inquiry as an ordinary new admission, in which case the admission form is sent as usual (BR-12).

alternateFlows.condition: The matched record was struck off rather than simply left
alternateFlows.behaviour: The striking-off and its reason are carried onto the inquiry, so the Principal sees it before approving (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: An outstanding balance is carried from the previous enrolment
alternateFlows.behaviour: The balance is shown before the decision. The Principal decides with it in view; how it is settled is a fee matter, not an admission one (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: A staff member records the re-admission enquiry by phone or in person
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Add New Inquiry → Re-admission
alternateFlows.behaviour: The same fields are captured on the internal screen, and the source is stamped Phone or Walk-in rather than Online Form.

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian's contact changed while the family was away
alternateFlows.behaviour: The new number is captured and replaces the guardian's sign-in contact on approval. The previous value stays in the audit trail (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The matched student transferred to another branch rather than leaving
alternateFlows.behaviour: Re-admission is refused here and inter-branch transfer is the correct path (BR-10).

exceptions.condition: The previous student ID matches no record
exceptions.systemResponse: The inquiry is still created and flagged for the reviewer to resolve (BR-12).
exceptions.messageShown: We could not find that student ID. You can still submit, and the school will check it.

exceptions.condition: The matched record is currently enrolled
exceptions.messageShown: This student is currently enrolled in Grade 5 Section A. This is not a re-admission.

exceptions.condition: The matched record's name and date of birth differ from the inquiry
exceptions.systemResponse: The difference is shown field by field and the match is not confirmed automatically.
exceptions.messageShown: The details on this inquiry do not match the record for STD-2022-0451. Check before confirming.

exceptions.condition: A Staff user attempts to confirm the match
exceptions.messageShown: Only a School Admin can confirm a re-admission match.

exceptions.condition: The return section is at capacity
exceptions.systemResponse: The re-admission is not completed into it.
exceptions.messageShown: Section A is full. Choose another section, or approve without a section and place the student later.

exceptions.condition: The section filled while the decision was pending
exceptions.messageShown: Section A filled while this was awaiting approval. Choose another section.

exceptions.systemResponse: No enrolment is created, the record stays at Re-admission in progress, and nothing partial is left behind.
exceptions.messageShown: The re-admission could not be completed. The record is unchanged.

exceptions.condition: The matched student transferred to another branch
exceptions.messageShown: This student transferred to the Johar Town branch. Use inter-branch transfer instead.

Marking a student as left in the first place
Settling or writing off the carried balance

departures.requirement: Reactivation never rewrites or merges previous enrolment rows. The gap is preserved and visible on the record.
Reactivation, the closure of the previous enrolment and the new enrolment commit together or not at all.
The former-student match returns within 2 seconds, so the family is not left waiting on the public form.

openQuestions.question: How long after leaving may a child be re-admitted onto the same record?
openQuestions.assumption: No limit. The record is theirs.

openQuestions.question: Does a struck-off student need a higher approval than one who simply left?
openQuestions.assumption: Same approval, with the striking-off shown to the Principal (BR-8). Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Must a re-admitted student sit the admission test again, or may the school waive it?
openQuestions.assumption: They sit it. The feature routes them to scheduling like any other applicant.

openQuestions.question: Should the carried balance block the re-admission, or only be shown?
openQuestions.assumption: Only shown. Settling it is a fee matter.

openQuestions.question: Are the original student ID and roll number always kept, even after several years?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.
